meta.title: Jathag — Know your chart, not just your sign.
meta.description: Accurate Vedic birth charts, explained in short, honest, modern language. Free, no account, no ads. Beta, stars are being aligned.

betaBand: Jathag Beta. The stars are still aligning: we are actively refining our features and design.

hero.title: Know your chart, [not just your sign].
hero.intro: Jathag turns your birth details into an [accurate Vedic birth chart], and soon explains it in [short, honest, modern language].

features.title: An accurate chart
features.text: From your exact birth date, time and place, drawn in the style you know.

features.title: Your life timeline
features.text: The chapters of your life, your dasha periods, with where you are today.

features.title: Plain-language explanations
features.text: Short, honest notes on what each part means. No jargon, no fear.

editing.line: Editing {name}. See my chart saves your changes.

time.label: Time of birth
time.hint: As written on the birth record. 12 AM = midnight · 12 PM = noon.

place.label: Place of birth
place.hintAbove: Type your town or city, e.g. Hyderabad.
place.hintBelow: To narrow it down, add the state or country after a comma: Hyderabad, Telangana.
place.noResults: No places found. Try another spelling or a nearby town.
place.resultsCount: {count} places found. Use the up and down arrow keys to choose one.
place.resultsCountOne: 1 place found. Use the up and down arrow keys to choose it.
place.setAside: Not used: the coordinates in Advanced settings are used instead.

chartStyle.label: Chart style
chartStyle.northNote: North Indian drawing arrives with the new chart page. Showing South Indian for now.

manual.hint: Decimal degrees. Use a minus sign for South or West.
manual.timeZoneHint: The UTC offset of the clock the birth time was written on.

clock.legend: Which clock was the time written on?

sentences.mumbai: In Mumbai until the 1950s, many families used Bombay time, 39 minutes behind IST. If you're not sure, keep IST.
sentences.westBengal: In Kolkata and West Bengal until the late 1940s, many families used Calcutta time, 23 minutes 20 seconds ahead of IST. If you're not sure, keep IST.
sentences.warTime: From September 1942 to October 1945 India's official clock was War Time, one hour ahead of IST. If you're not sure, keep War Time.
sentences.warTimeEarly: Between October 1941 and May 1942 some parts of India used War Time, one hour ahead of IST. If you're not sure, keep IST.
sentences.before1906: Before 1906, many towns kept their own local time, here about {minutes} minutes {direction} IST. If you're not sure, keep IST.
sentences.before1906OneMinute: Before 1906, many towns kept their own local time, here about 1 minute {direction} IST. If you're not sure, keep IST.
sentences.before1906Same: Before 1906, many towns kept their own local time; here it was within a minute of IST. If you're not sure, keep IST.
sentences.mumbaiWarTime: From September 1942 to October 1945 India's official clock was War Time, one hour ahead of IST, and in Mumbai many families also used Bombay time, 39 minutes behind IST. If you're not sure, keep War Time.
sentences.mumbaiWarTimeEarly: Between October 1941 and May 1942 some parts of India used War Time, one hour ahead of IST, and in Mumbai many families used Bombay time, 39 minutes behind IST. If you're not sure, keep IST.
sentences.westBengalWarTime: From September 1942 to October 1945 India's official clock was War Time, one hour ahead of IST, and in Kolkata and West Bengal many families also used Calcutta time, 23 minutes 20 seconds ahead of IST. If you're not sure, keep War Time.
sentences.westBengalWarTimeEarly: Between October 1941 and May 1942 some parts of India used War Time, one hour ahead of IST, and in Kolkata and West Bengal many families used Calcutta time, 23 minutes 20 seconds ahead of IST. If you're not sure, keep IST.

certainty.legend: How sure are you of the birth time?
certainty.partOfDay: Or pick a part of the day:
certainty.roughText: We'll show what stays the same across these two hours and what could differ. A narrow range gives a clearer chart.

repeatedTime.question: This time happened twice that night: the clocks went back an hour. Which one was it?
repeatedTime.later: The second time (after the clocks went back)

unreachable.title: We couldn't reach the calculator
unreachable.text: Your connection may have dropped for a moment. Your details are still in the form, so nothing is lost.

clockNote.buttonLabel: About the clock used for this date
clockNote.mumbai: In Mumbai until the 1950s, many people used Bombay time, 39 minutes behind IST. We've calculated your chart with IST. If your family used Bombay time, your chart may be different.
clockNote.westBengal: In Kolkata and West Bengal until the late 1940s, many people used Calcutta time, 23 minutes 20 seconds ahead of IST. We've calculated your chart with IST. If your family used Calcutta time, your chart may be different.
clockNote.warTime: From September 1942 to October 1945 India's official clock was War Time, one hour ahead of IST, and we've used it. If the time was written in IST, your chart may be different.
clockNote.warTimeEarly: Between October 1941 and May 1942 some parts of India used War Time, one hour ahead of IST. We've calculated your chart with IST. If the time was written in War Time, your chart may be different.
clockNote.before1906: Before 1906, many towns kept their own local time. Here that was about {minutes} minutes {direction} IST. We've calculated your chart with IST. If the time was written in local time, your chart may be different.
clockNote.before1906OneMinute: Before 1906, many towns kept their own local time. Here that was about 1 minute {direction} IST. We've calculated your chart with IST. If the time was written in local time, your chart may be different.
clockNote.before1906Same: Before 1906, many towns kept their own local time. Here it was within a minute of IST, so your chart is very unlikely to change. We've calculated your chart with IST.
clockNote.mumbaiWarTime: From September 1942 to October 1945 India's official clock was War Time, one hour ahead of IST, and we've used it. In Mumbai, many people also used Bombay time, 39 minutes behind IST. If the time was written in IST or in Bombay time, your chart may be different.
clockNote.mumbaiWarTimeEarly: Between October 1941 and May 1942 some parts of India used War Time, one hour ahead of IST, and in Mumbai many people used Bombay time, 39 minutes behind IST. We've calculated your chart with IST. If the time was written in War Time or in Bombay time, your chart may be different.
clockNote.westBengalWarTime: From September 1942 to October 1945 India's official clock was War Time, one hour ahead of IST, and we've used it. In Kolkata and West Bengal, many people also used Calcutta time, 23 minutes 20 seconds ahead of IST. If the time was written in IST or in Calcutta time, your chart may be different.
clockNote.westBengalWarTimeEarly: Between October 1941 and May 1942 some parts of India used War Time, one hour ahead of IST, and in Kolkata and West Bengal many people used Calcutta time, 23 minutes 20 seconds ahead of IST. We've calculated your chart with IST. If the time was written in War Time or in Calcutta time, your chart may be different.
clockNote.choosePlaceFirst: Once you've chosen the place, you can change the clock in Advanced settings.
clockNote.chosen: You've chosen {clock} ({offset}) in Advanced settings, so your chart will use that clock.
clockNote.before1906NoPlace: Before 1906, many towns kept their own local time, up to about half an hour different from IST. We've calculated your chart with IST. If the time was written in local time, your chart may be different.
